# W0303: `if let` that always matches

The pattern matches every value, so the first block always runs with the whole value bound. To match what an `Option` holds, write `if let Some(x) = …`; to bind the value, write `let`.

- Rule: [`expressions.if-let-always`](../../reference/08-expressions.md#expressions.if-let-always)
- Reported at: the pattern.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `warnings` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt W0303:2
fn first_or_zero(xs: List<i64>) -> i64 {
  if let x = xs.first() { x else 0 } else { 0 }
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn first_or_zero(xs: List<i64>) -> i64 {
  if let Some(x) = xs.first() { x } else { 0 }
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`W0303_if_let_that_always_matches.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/W0303_if_let_that_always_matches.lt):

```text
── `if let` THAT ALWAYS MATCHES ── W0303_if_let_that_always_matches.lt:3:10  [W0303]

This pattern matches every value, so the block always runs:

  3 │   if let x = xs.first() { print("first: {x}") }
    │          ^

The pattern matches every value, so the first block always runs with the whole
value bound. To match what an `Option` holds, write `if let Some(x) = …`; to
bind the value, write `let`.

To fix it, match what the `Option` holds:

  3 │   if let Some(x) = xs.first() { print("first: {x}") }
    │          +++++ +
```
